_comment: Fictional sample confessions for Let's Spill demo mode. No real people, schools or companies.

confessions.text: I've been having an emotional affair with a colleague for a year. Nothing physical has happened, but I check my phone for their messages before I check on my partner. I know exactly what this is, and I don't know how to stop.
I still keep the train ticket from our first date in my wallet. We broke up two years ago. I've moved cities, changed wallets twice, and every time I transfer the ticket over like it's my ID.
I've been 'working remotely from the office' for three months. Nobody noticed I moved my desk to the empty corner by the plants. It's the most productive I've ever been.
I pretended to understand calculus for an entire semester. I nodded so convincingly that classmates started asking me for help. I learned it the night before the final by teaching it to them.
My best friend thinks I forgot her birthday this year. I didn't. I've been planning a surprise trip for six months and pretending to be clueless is the hardest acting job of my life.
My parents think I quit piano at fourteen. I didn't. I play on the old keyboard at my aunt's place every Sunday. I'm not ready to let them hear how much I missed it.
I water my neighbour's plants while they travel. I've started talking to them. The fern is my favourite and I feel a little guilty about that.
My partner cheated two years ago and I forgave them. I thought I'd moved on. Last week I caught myself reading their messages while they slept, and I hated who I'd become.
I said 'I love you' first and he said 'thank you'. We've been married eleven years now and I still bring it up at every anniversary dinner.
I accidentally replied-all with a cat meme to a company-wide budget email. Instead of an apology, I got four promotions-worth of reactions. My manager still calls me 'the morale officer'.
I've been secretly seeing a therapist for six months. Nobody in my life knows. It's the only hour of the week where I don't pretend I'm fine.
I failed my driving test three times and told everyone I was 'just choosing not to drive'. I passed on the fourth try last month and still haven't told anyone.
There's a friend I've been slowly drifting from and I don't know if I should fix it or let it go. We haven't argued. We just don't laugh at the same things anymore.
My younger brother thinks he taught himself to ride a bike. I was running behind him holding the seat for twenty minutes. I let go and never told him.
I cancelled plans tonight, put on clean sheets, made soup and read for four hours. Best evening I've had all year and I'm not sorry.
I've been seeing someone for two months and I still don't know if we're exclusive. I'm too scared to ask in case the answer changes everything.

Our team lead is having an affair with someone in another department and the whole floor knows except their spouse, who brings lunch every Friday. I don't know whether staying quiet makes me kind or a coward.
I applied for my own manager's job when she left and got it. Now I sit in her old chair and realise how much she protected us from. I owe her an apology I don't know how to give.
In my final year I wrote anonymous encouraging notes and left them in library books. Last week a stranger at a café told me a note in a library book got her through exams.
I lied about liking hiking to fit into a new friend group. Two years later I genuinely love it and they're my closest people. Sometimes the fake-it part works.
Every time my grandmother asks if I've eaten, I say no, even if I have. It's the only way she'll sit down with me for an hour.
I've had the same 'New Year' goal for six years: learn to swim. This summer I finally did it. I'm thirty-four and I cried in the shallow end.
I almost texted my ex last night after seeing our song in a playlist. I typed it, deleted it and texted my sister instead. Small victories.
I'm the person who refills the office coffee machine before anyone gets in. Nobody knows it's me and I'd like to keep it that way.
I switched majors in my third year and told my family it was a 'scheduling issue'. I graduate in spring with a degree they still don't know I'm doing.
I'm terrified of starting over at thirty, but I handed in my notice today anyway. Writing it here makes it feel real.
My friend asked me to be honest about her business idea. I was. She hasn't replied in a week. I'm still not sure honesty was the kind thing.
Dad and I don't talk about feelings, but every time I visit he fills my car's tank without saying anything. I think that's how he says it.
